projP1: Persephone was born from the desire to restore Milan's memory of its Navigli — a waterway system that defined the city's identity for centuries, progressively buried between 1929 and 1930.
projP2: Through augmented reality, AI, and historical photographs, we want to allow anyone to see Milan as it was — walking exactly where those who lived it walked.
welcP1: Explore Milan through the centuries. Persephone allows you to discover the city's historical sites, relive the past, and interact with history in a completely new way.
welcCard1Desc: Ask for historical information about the Navigli, neighbourhoods, and historical figures of Milan. A voice from the past, always with you.
welcCard2Desc: Activate augmented reality and watch the Naviglio reborn right before your eyes, exactly where you stand.
welcCard3Desc: Challenge yourself: find exactly where a 19th-century photograph was taken. The GPS will be your judge.
welcHint: Tap the map to explore historical places
gameSignals: While you walk, three signals guide you:
gameSoundDesc: A ticking sound becomes faster and higher-pitched as you get closer to the exact spot. When it turns into a continuous beep, you are right there.
gameVisDesc: The photo border changes colour — from blue to green — and pulses with a glow when you are close. When it turns fully green and steady, you've arrived.
gameTextDesc: A proximity label tells you in words how far you are: from 'Far' all the way to 'You are here!'. Trust it and keep walking.
navigliP1: For centuries, Milan was a city of water. Its {canali} formed one of the most sophisticated hydraulic networks in medieval Europe, used to transport goods, drain fields and supply the city. The {navigli} — the great artificial waterways — were the lifeblood of commerce: barges loaded with marble, grain and construction materials came and went constantly. It was {leonardo} himself who redesigned the system of locks in the 1490s, making it possible to raise boats between different water levels.
navigliP2: The {viadacqua} was not merely infrastructure — it was the beating heart of Milanese daily life. Washerwomen worked on the banks, taverns opened directly onto the water, and the docks buzzed with merchants from across Europe. Then, between 1929 and 1930, the city decided to bury it all. Under the new asphalt now lie centuries of history.
persephoneP1: Like {persefone} who descended to the underworld and returned, our project brings the buried {navigli} back to the surface. Through augmented reality and artificial intelligence, we overlay the past onto the present: you walk through today's streets and, through your phone, you see what once was.
persephoneP2: We built this experience for those who believe that a city's memory is not just in its monuments, but in the very ground beneath your feet. Point your camera at the buildings around you and let history speak.
howToARDesc: Point your camera at the surrounding buildings to activate the AR reconstruction.
howToPhotosDesc: Explore historical photos of each location and compare them with how they look today.
howToPlayDesc: Find the exact spot where a 19th-century photograph was taken — guided by sound, colour and GPS.
easterCanaliText: Milan once had more canals than Venice. Over 150 km of waterways crossed the city, connecting it to the Po valley and the rest of northern Italy.
easterNavigliText: The Naviglio Grande dates back to 1179. It took over two centuries to complete — one of the greatest engineering feats of the Middle Ages.
easterLeonardoText: Leonardo da Vinci redesigned the mitre gate locks around 1490, solving the problem of raising and lowering boats across different water levels. His design is still used in canals worldwide today.
easterViadacquaText: The decision to cover the Navigli was made in 1929 under the Fascist regime. Mussolini wanted wide modern avenues in Milan's centre. Today, proposals to uncover them resurface every few years.
easterPersefoneText: In Greek mythology, Persephone was the goddess who descended into the underworld and returned every spring — a symbol of cyclical rebirth. Like her, we bring what was buried back into the light.
gameRule1Desc: Take a close look at the vintage image of the place you are visiting.
gameRule2Desc: Physically go to the precise location where the original photograph was taken.
gameRule3Desc: When you think you’ve reached the right spot, press the "I'm here!" button.
gameRule4Desc: The system will check your position via GPS. To win the challenge, you must be within {dist} meters of the exact point.
